title: The Door That Opens Tomorrow
subtitle: Episode 01 · A signal from a ship that hasn't arrived yet.

nodes.title: A ship that isn't here
paragraphs: Dock Seven is asking to open. Which is strange, because Dock Seven is empty.

Through the wide station window, the planet Pel hangs like a rust-red marble. On the arrival board, the courier ship Wren is listed for TOMORROW, 09:40. But your wrist radio crackles with a voice about your age: “Whatever you do, don't open Dock Seven.”
Then the station announces a glass storm in ten minutes. You are Starport Nine's youngest navigation cadet. Naturally, every adult is too busy to notice the impossible message.

choices.label: Go see what's outside Dock Seven
choices.detail: Check the door before anyone opens it.

choices.label: Check the arrival board in Control
choices.detail: Find out where the message came from.

choices.label: Search the station's old records
choices.detail: You remember a story about the glass storms.

nodes.title: Three knocks
paragraphs: Dock Seven's warning light flashes amber. Nothing moves beyond its little round window. Then comes a sound from the other side of the door: knock, knock ... knock.
Ren, your friend from the repair crew, is balanced on a ladder with a wrench between their teeth. “Please tell me you heard that,” they say.

choices.label: Count the knocks
choices.detail: A pattern could mean something.

choices.label: Open the service panel
choices.detail: Find out what's powering the empty dock.

choices.label: Get Ren to help
choices.detail: Two heads, one impossible door.

nodes.title: The arrival that hasn't happened
paragraphs: Every screen in Control says the same thing: WREN / INBOUND. The recorded arrival time keeps changing, but it always lands on tomorrow.
TAVI, the station computer, speaks through a ceiling grille. “I would call this a mistake,” it says, “except mistakes usually stop when I ask nicely.”

choices.label: Open the passenger manifest
choices.detail: Learn who will be aboard the Wren.

choices.label: Trace the radio frequency
choices.detail: Use some power to pull the message apart.

choices.label: Tell Chief Osei what you found
choices.detail: Ask for help instead of sneaking around.

nodes.title: Dusty files, fresh trouble
paragraphs: The Archive smells like warm plastic and very old paper. The shelves hold navigation maps from before Starport Nine got its name.
A bookmark sticks out of a notebook titled THE GLASS STORMS: NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT (REVISED). That seems a little too reassuring.

choices.label: Read the storm notebook
choices.detail: Something here matches the warning.

choices.label: Unfold the old dock map
choices.detail: Find a way behind Dock Seven.

choices.label: Find the retired pilot in the Archive
choices.detail: They might remember an older docking system.

nodes.title: A message in metal
paragraphs: You tap the same rhythm against the hatch. The answer comes almost at once: three fast knocks and one slow one.
Ren points to a tiny service sticker. Three-fast-one-slow is an old Wren-class distress code. A person—or something pretending to be one—knows the rules.

choices.label: Write down the full rhythm
choices.detail: Bring the evidence to the central hall.

choices.label: Tell Ren everything
choices.detail: You'd rather have an ally than a secret.

nodes.title: An old switch
paragraphs: Inside the panel, cables have been reconnected in a hurry. One is warm. That shouldn't be possible: Dock Seven has been shut for months.
There's a handwritten label on the power junction. It reads: GUIDANCE MIRROR. NOT A DOOR CONTROL. Someone has crossed out the second sentence.

choices.label: Rewire the mirror sensor
choices.detail: Spend a power cell to read its last command.

choices.label: Patch the old speaker
choices.detail: Let whoever is sending the message hear you.

nodes.title: A better plan with two people
paragraphs: Ren looks from the sealed hatch to the clock above it. “I can help, but we're going to need a plan that doesn't start with opening a mysterious door.”
They pull a small repair drone from their bag. Its sticker says 'DO NOT TEACH ME TRICKS.' You suspect Ren wrote the sticker.

choices.label: Agree to work as a team
choices.detail: Ren promises to back your call.

choices.label: Ask Ren for a spare power cell
choices.detail: You'll have more options at the docking console.

nodes.title: Tomorrow's passengers
paragraphs: The Wren's passenger list includes three scientists, a crate of seedlings, and a junior pilot called Mika Vale. Their age is listed as thirteen.
The timestamp is the strange part: the list was signed tomorrow morning. Even the captain's signature is there. There is no mention of a distress call.

choices.label: Compare the signatures with the clock
choices.detail: The message is traveling backward through the storm.

choices.label: Forward the manifest to Chief Osei
choices.detail: A little proof goes a long way.

nodes.title: The voice in the static
paragraphs: TAVI strips away the hiss. The warning becomes clear. Behind it you hear a different sound: the cheerful chime from tomorrow's Wren departure announcement.
“This signal traveled in a circle,” TAVI says. “Time is behaving like a badly folded map.”

choices.label: Measure the signal's delay
choices.detail: You find a pattern in the storm's pulse.

choices.label: Disconnect the analyzer and save its charge
choices.detail: Keep enough power for the final decision.

nodes.title: An adult who listens
paragraphs: Chief Osei folds their arms. “A distress signal from tomorrow? That's a new one.” Then they read the arrival board for themselves.
“All right, cadet. I'll give you nine minutes. But you don't open a hatch until we know what's on the other side.”

choices.label: Explain what you know
choices.detail: Keep the chief on your side.

choices.label: Ask to see the sealed dock logs
choices.detail: Search quietly for the missing detail.

nodes.title: When light takes the long way
paragraphs: The notebook's author drew a radio wave wrapping around the station's metal ring. During a glass storm, the ring can bounce a signal from the next day into the present.
Under the diagram is a warning: THE DOCKING MIRROR IS NOT A HARMLESS REFLECTOR. IF MISALIGNED, IT POINTS SHIPS TOWARD THE ICE RING.

choices.label: Copy the storm-frequency numbers
choices.detail: Numbers could help you adjust the beacon.

choices.label: Trace the old mirror's wiring
choices.detail: Locate the backup power line.

nodes.title: The tunnel nobody uses
paragraphs: The old map shows a maintenance duct behind Dock Seven. It was bricked up on the newer maps, but Ren once told you that 'bricked up' usually means 'still opens if you kick it right.'
You mark the route on your wrist screen. It passes a narrow chamber where the mirror's repair drones are stored.

choices.label: Memorize the maintenance route
choices.detail: You can try the duct from the central hall.

choices.label: Send Ren the coordinates
choices.detail: Now someone else knows the way.

nodes.title: The pilot's old mistake
paragraphs: Pilot Juno is sitting in the Archive with a cup of tea and a model of the first Wren. They listen to your story without laughing.
“We used to guide ships with a mirror on the outer ring,” Juno says. “If it points even a little wrong during a storm, it looks like a safe dock where there's only empty space.”

choices.label: Ask how to fix the mirror
choices.detail: Learn the old piloting trick.

choices.label: Ask Juno to call Control
choices.detail: One more grown-up who believes you.

nodes.title: The last seven minutes
paragraphs: The station lights dim. A thin silver line crawls over the observation window: the first edge of the glass storm.
TAVI speaks through every hallway speaker. “Dock Seven is receiving a ship's signal. There is no ship outside. Both facts are true.” The guidance mirror starts turning on its own.
One more investigation might give you the missing piece. Or you could head straight for the docking console.

choices.label: Speak directly to the voice
choices.detail: Ask the person in tomorrow what they know.

choices.label: Climb to the antenna
choices.detail: Read the storm before the mirror locks.

choices.label: Follow the maintenance duct
choices.detail: Reach the repair drones without the main hall.

choices.label: Use the manual service path
choices.detail: A messy shortcut, but it will work.

choices.label: Find Chief Osei
choices.detail: Get someone with authority on your side.

choices.label: Go to the docking console now
choices.detail: It's almost time to make the call.

nodes.title: The kid aboard the Wren
paragraphs: “Hello?” you say into the radio. “My name doesn't matter. Are you on the Wren?”

“I'm Mika,” says the voice. “I haven't left Pel yet. At least, I don't think I have. I can see Starport Nine, but the dock lights are pointing toward the ice ring. We sent the warning before—” The voice crackles. “Before what?”
You hear a breath. “Before we followed them.”

choices.label: Ask Mika for proof
choices.detail: Check if the signal really is from tomorrow.

choices.label: Promise to correct the guidance lights
choices.detail: Sometimes being believed matters most.

nodes.title: Tomorrow can hear you
paragraphs: Mika reads you an equipment code that hasn't been assigned yet. TAVI checks, pauses, then says, “That code will be printed tomorrow at 07:10. I dislike admitting this, but I believe them.”
Mika laughs, a little shakily. “So if you fix the lights today, I won't have to send this warning tomorrow?”
TAVI doesn't answer. There isn't time to find out.

choices.label: Save the future equipment code
choices.detail: Every detail might help you steer the mirror.

choices.label: Share Mika's warning with the crew
choices.detail: Get everyone working on the same plan.

nodes.title: Above the red planet
paragraphs: From the antenna platform the storm looks like silver scratches across the stars. You can feel the platform hum through your boots.
The guidance mirror is pointing two degrees toward the ice ring. Not much. More than enough. A red dial ticks toward zero.

choices.label: Adjust the mirror using the storm pulse
choices.detail: The signal should point away from the ice.

choices.label: Bank the antenna's last power cell
choices.detail: You may need a bigger pulse later.

nodes.title: Small enough to fit
paragraphs: The maintenance duct is barely wide enough for you. At its end is a storage rack holding four ancient repair drones. Three are dead. The fourth wakes when you touch its scratched blue shell.
A message blinks on its screen: I REMEMBER THE SAFE WAY. Its tiny thrusters cough out a puff of dust.

choices.label: Bring the drone online
choices.detail: It might be able to guide the ship itself.

choices.label: Download its route map
choices.detail: Use the old flight path to aim the beacon.

nodes.title: No more secrets
paragraphs: Chief Osei is already at the docking console. They read your notes without interrupting.
“I believe you,” they say at last. “I'll keep the corridor clear. You make the call about the lights. But remember: a door can stay closed while a signal travels through it.”

choices.label: Request full control of the guidance mirror
choices.detail: You'll need help to carry out a risky plan.

choices.label: Ask everyone to hold the dock shutters
choices.detail: Buy the Wren another chance to find the right signal.

nodes.title: The mirror turns
paragraphs: The console counts down: SIXTY SECONDS TO STORM LOCK. Beyond the window is empty space—and somewhere in tomorrow, a ship full of people who think this is their way home.
You can leave the dock sealed. You can try a new course. You can send a warning that might change tomorrow. But you cannot choose everything.
TAVI leaves one line on the screen: YOUR CALL, CADET.

choices.label: Build a path through the storm
choices.detail: Combine the evidence, station power, and crew cooperation.

choices.label: Redirect the outer guidance beacon
choices.detail: A safe route, but you may lose contact with the Wren.

choices.label: Send the old repair drone
choices.detail: Let a small machine find the way.

choices.label: Send tomorrow a new warning
choices.detail: Trust that Mika can act on what you tell them.

choices.label: Seal Dock Seven and alert tomorrow's crew
choices.detail: The cautious choice isn't always the wrong one.

choices.label: Open Dock Seven to find out what's there
choices.detail: Maybe the message meant something else.

nodes.title: A bridge across tomorrow
paragraphs: You send the storm's rhythm to Mika, give Chief Osei the safe coordinates, and fire one clean pulse through the guidance mirror.
For a moment the red planet appears doubled. Then tomorrow's Wren answers. “We see the real dock,” Mika says. “We see you.”

The following morning the Wren arrives exactly on time, with three scientists, a crate of seedlings, and a junior pilot who looks straight at you and grins. No one can explain how yesterday's conversation happened. You don't mind. You have questions for tomorrow.

nodes.title: A light in the wrong place
paragraphs: You turn the outer beacon away from the ice ring. The station's lights blink out for seven long seconds. Then they return—and Dock Seven falls quiet.
Tomorrow the Wren comes in on a wide, safe loop. It takes longer, but everyone gets home. Mika sends you a message as soon as the ship docks: “Did you hear me yesterday? I think you did.”
Some mysteries don't need a neat answer to end well.

ending.title: A light in the wrong place

nodes.title: The smallest pilot
paragraphs: The drone shoots into the storm like a blue pebble with opinions. Its old navigation chip remembers a path the station computers forgot.
Static fills the radio. Then a tinny voice from the drone says, “LEFT. NO, YOUR OTHER LEFT.” You hear Mika laugh.
The Wren arrives tomorrow with a small scrape on its hull and all its passengers safe. Ren insists the drone gets its own medal. You agree, though you suggest a new sticker: DO TEACH ME TRICKS.

nodes.title: Message received
paragraphs: You send Mika everything you know: the ice ring, the mirror angle, and the one course to avoid. The warning disappears into the shining storm.
Tomorrow, before launch, the station receives a short reply from the Wren. “We changed our approach. Thank you.”
Chief Osei says you may have just rewritten a piece of history. TAVI calls it an unverified hypothesis. You call it a good day.

ending.title: Message received
ending.note: You changed the plan, not the past.

nodes.title: The door stays shut
paragraphs: You lock the empty dock and send an urgent navigation warning for tomorrow's flight. The guidance mirror stops turning. The station rides out the storm.
No one on Starport Nine is hurt. Tomorrow's launch is delayed while the engineers inspect the old mirror, and the Wren lands a day late with everyone aboard.
You never find out who sent the first message. But sometimes the bravest answer to a strange door is: not yet.

ending.title: The door stays shut
ending.note: You chose patience over a gamble.

nodes.title: Nothing on the other side
paragraphs: You hit OPEN. The door rolls aside, revealing only the safety field and the stars beyond it. The rushing noise isn't air; it's radio static, pouring through the guidance mirror.
For an instant you see a shadow of the Wren—then it's gone. The station shuts down the mirror automatically. Tomorrow the engineers ground the ship for inspection, and no one is harmed.
TAVI files the incident under DOORS / UNWISE. Ren thinks that's unfair. You think maybe the message was worth listening to.
